collision_verdict: A single cwd file `.tmux-agent-result` is not acceptable as the canonical fix: multiple workers can and do share one repo cwd, while result paths are per-agent under `agent_root_dir()/name/result.json`. Last-start-wins clobbering would make a worker write another worker's result. `--workdir-fresh` avoids the collision only when explicitly used; it cannot be required for normal pair/fanout/review flows, resume, or start-ssh.
blocking_concerns: Option A has a correctness blocker unless it is redesigned away from a single cwd filename. Per-agent files still need the agent name inside the sandbox, so they collapse back into a prompt/locator problem.

Option B is safer than A for local `start`, but codex-only initial-prompt injection is incomplete for codex-family profiles and later `send`/`send-wait` turns; `resume` currently launches the CLI without a new task prompt.

The real code has no env-independent result-path fallback today: `apply_result_env_args` only appends `TMUX_AGENT_NAME` and `TMUX_AGENT_RESULT` as tmux session env, and docs already warn sandboxed agent tools cannot expand `$TMUX_AGENT_RESULT`.
minimal_interface: For local codex-family sessions, automatically append a short result contract to every user task boundary that sends prompt text (`start` initial text, `send`, `send-wait`, and `send-wait-literal`): `Write final JSON to this exact path: <absolute result_path>`. Compute that path from the existing `agent_root_dir()/name/result.json`; do not add user-facing flags. Keep `result --path <name>` as the manual/debug surface.
